registry_notes: Vetted vs scikit-image regionprops: NYXUS == 90 - degrees(skimage.orientation) = 70.4174 (row-axis vs x-axis convention); matches to 10 decimals because the ellipse angle is invariant to the pixel-size second-moment correction that makes MAJOR/MINOR/ECCENTRICITY differ ~1.4%. gen_morphology_skimage.py

Tier-2 documented-formula conformance, NO external oracle. Nyxus computes ROUNDNESS = 4*A/(pi*major^2) (ellipse_fitting.cpp) with A = ROI pixel count and major = moment-fit MAJOR_AXIS_LENGTH. TEST_2D_MORPHOLOGY_DOCUMENTED_FORMULA_CONFORMANCE_ANALYTIC (test_2d_morphology_analytic.h) recomputes the formula and requires an exact match (1e-9). Implementation bug-free, but the value depends on Nyxus' pixel-area + moment-fit conventions; no third-party tool reproduces it. Formula-vetted only.

registry_notes: Vetted vs imea 0.3.5 imea.measure_2d.macro.perimeter_equal_diameter -- a third-party implementation of the DIN ISO 9276-6 perimeter-equal diameter (perimeter/pi), the same documented transform Nyxus applies in contour.cpp. Fed the Nyxus PERIMETER (26.9349412836191) imea returns 8.57365809435588 vs Nyxus 8.57365809435587 (|diff| 1.07e-14), asserted at the exact tier in test_2d_morphology_imea.h. SCOPE: this vets the TRANSFORM, not the perimeter it consumes -- imea's own perimeter is cv2.arcLength (12.6569 vs Nyxus' chain-code 26.9349), so imea's END-TO-END diameter_equal_perimeter is 4.0288 and does NOT agree; the entire gap is inherited from PERIMETER, which stays regression. gen_morphology_imea.py

Tier-2 documented-formula conformance, NO external oracle. Nyxus computes CIRCULARITY = sqrt(4*pi*A)/P (convex_hull_nontriv.cpp) with A = ROI pixel count and P = contour perimeter. TEST_2D_MORPHOLOGY_DOCUMENTED_FORMULA_CONFORMANCE_ANALYTIC (test_2d_morphology_analytic.h) recomputes the formula from AREA_PIXELS_COUNT/PERIMETER and requires an exact match (1e-9), so the implementation is bug-free -- but the value is convention-specific (pixel-area + contour-perimeter) and no third-party tool reproduces it (pyradiomics/skimage use mesh area/perimeter). Formula-vetted only.

Vetted vs scikit-image 0.26.0: the oracle's filters are skimage.filters.gabor_kernel itself (freq=f0/2pi, sigma_x=sig2lam*2pi/f0, sigma_y=sigma_x/gamma, offset=0) cropped to the Nyxus 16x16 grid, and an independent reimplementation of the L1-norm/convolve/crop/score pipeline reproduces all 16 golden values exactly (max |diff| 0.000e+00 at rel=1e-3). gen_gabor_skimage.py. The kernel-parameter mapping is additionally cross-checked against the documented closed form (max |kernel diff| 1.7e-18 to 2.6e-18). SCOPE 1: the f0=0 baseline filter is the one kernel not taken from skimage -- gabor_kernel cannot take frequency=0; at f0=0 the envelope and the carrier are both identically 1, so that filter is the flat window in closed form. SCOPE 2: the GPU path is NOT vetted -- calculate_gpu (FFT convolution) diverges from the direct-convolution CPU path on these ROIs, a pre-existing discrepancy; the assertion covers the in-RAM CPU path only. REQUIRED a fix first: gabor.cpp stored the filter-response magnitudes as PixIntens (unsigned int), truncating sub-integer responses to 0; now kept real-valued (double CPU/nt, RealPixIntens GPU).

Two bugs fixed to get there: (1) laplacian() multiplied PixIntens (unsigned) by the negative kernel weights, wrapping to 2.81e18; (2) variance() took |x| before the variance, giving Var(|X|) instead of Var(X) -- 12.109 vs 34.957, 65% low, since zero padding keeps the Laplacian mean (-0.958 here) away from 0. SCOPE: ksize=1 only (the ksize>1 kernel has no cv2 counterpart and calculate() never selects it); out-of-core get_focus_score_NT not covered.
